comment: `$.color.primary.main` — a variable the project declared, which compiles to `var(--color-primary-main)`. Its own injection rather than a pattern in the hole grammar, because that file's name would then be wrong about half of what it does; the two share an injection SELECTOR because they are the same position — the things this language puts inside a CSS value. `-string` is not caution: a path is text inside `content: "…"`, and the CSS grammar's string scope is still inside a property value, so the injection would otherwise reach in and colour it.

variable.comment: The whole path is ONE token, and that is the point rather than a shortcut. Measured before this existed, on `color: $.color.primary.main`: the CSS grammar tokenised the segment `color` on its own and gave it `support.constant.property-value.css` — its KEYWORD colour — so a reader saw `color` glowing in the middle of a variable path with no way to know it meant nothing there. `size`, `content`, `border` and `grid` are all ordinary names for a group of variables, so the fault is common rather than contrived. A segment may begin with a digit (`2xl`, `0`): the block is this package's grammar, and only the virtual file has to be TypeScript. The `$` is coloured as this language's marker for the same reason `@@` is — one sigil, one meaning, wherever it appears.
